sources.title: Alan Warhaftig, “Don’t Be Afraid of Going Wrong: Conversations with C. L. R. James,” 2023
sources.citation: Alan Warhaftig, “Don’t Be Afraid of Going Wrong: Conversations with C. L. R. James,” Los Angeles Review of Books, 12 January 2023; edited interview excerpts recorded 12–13 November 1977 and 15 October 1976.

verification.note: Complete displayed original publication of the interviewer’s own conversations read, including date/recording/editorial introduction and both excerpts. First section 1977 concerns Britain, teaching and politics; second section 1976 concerns Minty Alley. Edited for length and clarity; original tapes and complete novel/monographs unread. Strong Thackeray, Constantine, Cardus, Robeson, Warburg and Selma reception leads retained, not erased by available endpoints. A discrete Ibn Khaldun teaching use is not a blanket formative influence.

sources.title: Rachel Douglas, “Unsilencing the Haitian Revolution: C. L. R. James and The Black Jacobins”
sources.citation: Rachel Douglas, “Unsilencing the Haitian Revolution: C. L. R. James and The Black Jacobins,” Atlantic Studies 19, no. 2 (2022): 281–304; first published online 19 November 2020.

verification.note: Actual author’s University of Glasgow repository copy of original publisher PDF, selected 281–285 and 286 through the Robeson collaboration and opening historical-drama paragraph, plus notes 1–25 at 297–298 read. Complete article not claimed. Online 2020 and issue 2022 dates distinct. Douglas’s scholarly mediation, archival work and conceptual comparison are attributed; complete James originals, scripts, original tapes, Trouillot/Fischer/Buck-Morss books and archival manuscript dedication not independently consulted.
